name: Generic Bulking Routine (GBR)
author: Lyle McDonald
summary: A 4-day upper/lower split that trains each muscle twice a week with heavy 6-8 rep sets followed by lighter 10-15 rep sets. It runs in 8-week cycles: two easier ramp-up weeks, then six weeks of adding weight, then you reset and go again.
evidenceNote: Lyle's 2020 article targets roughly 6-8 sets (40-70 reps) per muscle per session, trained twice a week and stopped 1-2 reps short of failure, which matches current hypertrophy evidence well. As written here (low end of each set range) it is about 5 hard sets per muscle per session (about 10 per week), rising to about 7 per session at the top of the ranges. Direct arm work is minimal (1-2 sets each of biceps and triceps per upper session), exercises are mostly left to the lifter, and JC Deen (not Lyle in the verified text) says it is not for beginners.

sources.title: A Look at Some Popular Hypertrophy Programs (Lyle McDonald, 2008, updated 2020)
Lyle McDonald's Bulking Routine (JC Deen, reproduces Lyle's forum post)

schedule: Mon Lower, Tue Upper, Thu Lower, Fri Upper. The Thu/Fri workouts either repeat Mon/Tue or use slight substitutions (e.g. a deadlift/leg press combo on Thursday; move incline and pulldown to the start of the second upper day). Doing each workout every 5th day is acceptable for people with poorer recovery. Session length is not stated; 75 min is an estimate.

progression.description: Uses Lyle's 2020-updated article as the current version, with the exercise template from his forum post as reproduced by JC Deen. 8-week cycle: 2 submaximal run-up weeks, then 6 weeks of trying to add weight to the bar as consistently as possible; then drop the weight and start a new cycle, aiming for a higher peak. Sets stop 1-2 reps short of failure (some will reach failure as fatigue builds). Add weight once you reach the top of the rep range (JC Deen's restatement; a reader quotes Lyle as adding weight when the first set reaches the top of the range with a rep or two to spare). No increment is specified.
progression.deload: Built into the cycle: after each 8-week cycle, drop the weights and start over. If the volume is too much, use 2-3x6-8 for the main lifts and 1-2x10-12 for the secondary lifts.
